title: Register a short-term rental (homestay): zoning permit or registry, business license and lodging tax
question: I want to rent my house or a room for stays of 30 days or less. What do I file with the city?
office: Commissioner of the Revenue, City of Staunton (an elected constitutional officer, who keeps the short-term rental registration and assesses the business license and lodging tax; the City Treasurer collects payments; the Zoning Administrator in the Planning & Zoning Division enforces the homestay zoning rules)
summary: Staunton requires short-term rental operators, owners or tenants, to register each property with the Commissioner of the Revenue within 30 days of first offering it, and again by March 1 each year. The Homestay Registration costs $50 per property a year and names a local responsible party on call 24/7; tenants need the owner's signature. It also feeds your business license (a $30 fee up to $50,000 of receipts in the contractor, retail, professional and business service classes; the City does not say which class a homestay is in). City zoning rules: stays of 30 days or less, no meals, guests 18 or older, two adults per bedroom, no signs, inspection on request. Charge the 6.7% lodging tax on direct bookings and file monthly by the 20th; platforms collect on theirs, and a host whose bookings all go through platforms may attest to that yearly instead. Not registering costs $500 per violation.

legal_basis.quote: "Short-term rental" means the provision of a room or space that is suitable or intended for occupancy for dwelling, sleeping, or lodging purposes, for a period of fewer than 30 consecutive days, in exchange for a charge for the occupancy.
any locality may, by ordinance, establish a short-term rental registry and require operators within the locality to register annually.

The registration shall be ministerial in nature and shall require the operator to provide (i) the complete name of the operator, (ii) the address of each property in the locality offered for short-term rental by the operator, and (iii) an attestation that the property owner has granted permission for use of such property as a short-term rental if the operator is a lessee or sublessee.
A locality may charge a reasonable fee for such registration related to the actual costs of establishing and maintaining the registry.
No ordinance shall require a person to register pursuant to this section if such person is (i) licensed by the Real Estate Board or is a property owner who is represented by a real estate licensee
such ordinance may include a penalty not to exceed $500 per violation for an operator required to register who offers for short-term rental a property that is not registered with the locality.
Such ordinance may provide that unless and until an operator pays the penalty and registers such property, the operator may not continue to offer such property for short-term rental.

Such ordinance may further provide that an operator required to register may be prohibited from offering a specific property for short-term rental in the locality upon multiple violations on more than three occasions of applicable state and local laws, ordinances, and regulations, as they relate to the short-term rental.

No local ordinance shall prohibit an operator from offering a property as a short-term rental solely on the basis that such operator is a lessee or sublessee, provided that the property owner has granted permission for such property's use as a short-term rental.

No local ordinance enacted after December 31, 2023, or any subsequent amendment, shall require that a special exception, special use, or conditional use permit be obtained for the use of a residential dwelling as a short-term rental where the dwelling unit is also legally occupied by the property owner as his primary residence.
nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit, limit, or otherwise supersede existing local authority to regulate the short-term rental of property through general land use and zoning authority.

Nothing in this section shall be construed to supersede or limit contracts or agreements between or among individuals or private entities related to the use of real property, including recorded declarations and covenants

legal_basis.citation: Staunton City Code § 3.37.020 (Staunton City Code ch. 3.37 (Registration for Short-Term Rental), as reproduced by the City on the back of its Homestay Registration form)
legal_basis.quote: “Short-term rental” means the provision of a room or space that is suitable or intended for occupancy for dwelling, sleeping, or lodging purposes, for a period of fewer than 30 consecutive days, in exchange for charge for the occupancy.

“Operator” means the proprietor of any dwelling, lodging, or sleeping accommodations offered as a short-term rental, whether in the capacity of the owner, lessee, sub-lessee, or mortgagee in possession, licensee, or any other possessory capacity.

A short-term rental operator shall within 30 days of holding or continuing to hold itself out as offering lodging to register with the Commissioner of the Revenue to allow for the assessment and remittance of business license as required under SCC §5.05.100 and transient occupancy taxes as provided in SCC §3.35.010.

After initial registration under the provision of this chapter, a short-term rental operator shall register by not later than March 1 each year with the Commissioner of Revenue, providing the complete name of the operator and the legal and street address (and parcel identification number) of each property in the City of Staunton offered for short-term rental by the operator.
The annual registration fee shall be fifty dollars ($50.00) for each property for which the operator is engaged in short-term rental and shall be paid to the City of Staunton.
There is imposed a penalty of $500.00 for each violation for any failure to register as required under the provision of this chapter.
Until an operator pays the penalty and registers such property as required under the provision of this chapter, the operator shall not offer or rent such property for short-term rental.
For any repeated violations of the provisions of this chapter as it relates to a specific property, the operator is prohibited from registering and offering that property for short-term rental.

An operator required to register under the provisions of this chapter is prohibited from offering a specific property for short-term rental in the City of Staunton upon multiple violations on more than three occasions of applicable state and local laws, ordinance, and regulations, as they relate to the short-term rental of such property.

Notwithstanding compliance with the provisions of this chapter, an operator shall comply with all other provisions of the Staunton City Code and other applicable law, including but not limited to those related to land use under Chapter 18.152 of Title 18 of the Staunton City Code.

legal_basis.citation: Staunton City Code § 18.152.020 (Staunton City Code ch. 18.152 (Homestay), as reproduced by the City on the back of its Homestay Registration form; the definition is also on the Commissioner's Business License & Taxes page)
legal_basis.quote: “Homestay” means the use of a residential dwelling unit or a portion thereof for occupancy for lodging purposes in exchange for charge for occupancy.

legal_basis.citation: Staunton City Code § 18.152.020 (homestay definition; the Commissioner of the Revenue's Business License & Taxes page gives the same words under the heading 'Homestay', without a section number)
legal_basis.quote: The duration of any period of occupancy may not exceed 30 days; however, there shall be no limit to the frequency in which rentals to occupants may occur.
Any operator utilizing a dwelling as a homestay shall be in violation unless the operator complies with the following requirements:
Shall only be rented on a daily or weekly basis.
No meals shall be prepared for or served to guests, and the guest for which the property is authorized for use shall be at least eighteen (18) years of age.
The homestay shall accommodate no more than two adult guests per bedroom.
No signs, advertising, or any other display on the property indication the use as a homestay shall be allowed.

At the request of the City of Staunton zoning administrator, operators shall grant the authority to enter the subject property, upon reasonable notice, at least one (1) time during the calendar year to verify compliance at the time with the provisions of this section.
A homestay shall be exempt from providing additional off-street parking required under the provisions of SCC 18.125.

steps.step: Check that you may host at the address, as owner or tenant
steps.who: Operator (owner, tenant or other person in possession)
steps.how: Staunton's rules apply to any operator: the owner, a tenant (lessee or sublessee), a mortgagee in possession, a licensee or anyone else in possession. The City Code text the City publishes has no owner-occupancy rule. A homestay is a land use under Title 18, and chapter 18.152 sets the conditions under which it is allowed. The district chapters checked (R-1 to R-4, TRD-1, TND-I, P-1, B-1, B-2, B-4 and B-5) do not mention homestays, and the Planning & Zoning permit list has no homestay permit. So ask Planning & Zoning, or request a Zoning Official Determination Letter ($75), whether a homestay is allowed at your address and whether any zoning permit is needed. The Commissioner may not issue a business license where zoning prohibits the business (City Code § 5.05.060, paraphrased). If you rent the home, get the owner's written permission: the owner signs the registration. Deeds, covenants and condominium or HOA rules can still ban rentals.
steps.quote: Notwithstanding compliance with the provisions of this chapter, an operator shall comply with all other provisions of the Staunton City Code and other applicable law, including but not limited to those related to land use under Chapter 18.152 of Title 18 of the Staunton City Code.

steps.step: Set up the rental to meet the homestay rules
steps.how: Rent by the day or week only, for stays of 30 days or less. Do not prepare or serve meals. Guests must be at least 18. Take no more than two adult guests per bedroom. Put up no sign, advertising or other display on the property. A homestay needs no extra off-street parking.
steps.quote: The homestay shall accommodate no more than two adult guests per bedroom.

steps.step: Name a local responsible party who can answer complaints at any hour
steps.who: Operator; the responsible party (a local person or business)
steps.how: Pick a person or business located locally who can respond to issues and complaints 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, in person if needed, while guests are staying. Their name, address, phones and email go on the registration form. Without one the Commissioner will not issue the business license. This requirement comes from the form: the printed chapter 3.37 does not mention a responsible party, and it is not among the items state law says a registry requires (Va. Code § 15.2-983(B)(1)).
steps.quote: A Business License will not be issued if no local Responsible Party is named.

steps.step: File the Homestay Registration with the Commissioner of the Revenue and pay $50 for each property
steps.how: Fill in the Homestay Registration form: applicant, property address, owner (if not you), and the responsible party. Sign it; the owner signs too if you are not the owner. By signing you agree to inspections by the Zoning Administrator. Mail it to P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402, fax it to (540) 851-4022, or email it to revenue@ci.staunton.va.us. The fee is $50 a year for each property, paid to the City of Staunton (the form's office box lists cash or check). State law exempts some operators, such as owners represented by a real estate licensee (Va. Code § 15.2-983(B)(2)); the City's text shows no exemptions, so ask the office.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of holding or continuing to hold itself out as offering lodging (City Code § 3.37.030(1))
steps.quote: A short-term rental operator shall within 30 days of holding or continuing to hold itself out as offering lodging to register with the Commissioner of the Revenue to allow for the assessment and remittance of business license as required under SCC §5.05.100 and transient occupancy taxes as provided in SCC §3.35.010.

steps.who: Operator; Commissioner of the Revenue (assesses and issues the license)
steps.how: The registration is used to assess your business license. The City publishes a Business License Application, and its rate table lists the Homestay Yearly Registration at $50.00. The pages do not say whether homestay hosts must also file that application. The safe course is to send it with the registration, giving your estimated gross receipts to December 31. For the contractor, retail, professional and business service classes the fee is $30 on gross receipts up to $50,000, with a rate per $100 above that; wholesale merchants and direct sellers are charged differently. No page says which class a homestay falls in, so ask the office. No license is issued while business license or personal property taxes owed to the City are unpaid (the City Code adds meals and transient occupancy taxes, among others: § 5.05.020(2), paraphrased), or where zoning prohibits the business (§ 5.05.060, paraphrased).
steps.deadline: City pages: within 30 days of when you begin to conduct business. State law and City Code § 5.05.100(2) (paraphrased): before beginning business (Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a))
steps.fee: $30 fee for gross receipts of $0-50,000 in the contractor, retail, professional and business service classes; above $50,000, the class rate per $100 of gross receipts
steps.quote: To avoid penalties and interest, you are required to file an application within 30 days of when you begin to conduct business.

steps.step: The Commissioner approves or denies the registration; the Zoning Administrator may check compliance
steps.who: Commissioner of the Revenue; Zoning Administrator (Planning & Zoning Division)
steps.how: The form's office box records the date received, Approved or Denied, the amount paid and the parcel number. State law makes registration ministerial and lists what it requires: the operator's full name, each property address, and the owner's permission if a tenant registers. At the Zoning Administrator's request you must let the Zoning Administrator enter, on reasonable notice, at least once each calendar year to check compliance (City Code § 18.152.030(5)). No time limit for the decision was found.
steps.quote: I give my consent to inspectors of the Zoning Administrator to verify compliance with current zoning requirements and grant a right of access to the Zoning Administrator to make such inspections.

steps.step: Register for the lodging tax and charge 6.7% on stays you book directly
steps.who: Operator for direct bookings; the platform (accommodations intermediary) for bookings it facilitates
steps.how: Staunton's transient occupancy (lodging) tax is 6.7%. Your registration also sets you up for it with the Commissioner of the Revenue. On a stay you book yourself, add the tax to the total price and show it separately on the bill or invoice. On a stay booked through Airbnb, VRBO or a similar platform, the platform collects the tax on the room charge and pays it to the City. City Code § 3.35.040 (read on eCode360, paraphrased) puts these duties on hosts and platforms in the same terms as state law.
steps.fee: 6.7% of the price paid for the stay
steps.quote: Those entities collecting such tax shall register with the Commissioner of the Revenue and file the proper returns.

steps.step: File the Transient/Occupancy Tax Return every month, with payment
steps.who: Operator; Commissioner of the Revenue (return); City Treasurer (payment)
steps.how: On the City's return, report the month's gross receipts from all lodging rentals. Deduct exempt rentals of more than 30 consecutive days and refunds. Multiply the net by 6.7%. List each platform with the receipts and the tax it paid for you, and attach the platform's transaction records. Without them you owe the tax yourself. Mail the return and a check payable to City of Staunton, Treasurer, to the Commissioner of the Revenue, P.O. Box 4, Staunton, VA 24402. If every booking goes through platforms, City Code § 3.35.050(6) (read on eCode360, paraphrased) lets you attest to that to the Commissioner instead of filing returns; the attestation lasts 12 months and is renewed yearly on a date and form the Commissioner sets (state law: Va. Code § 58.1-3827(D)). No City page or form read describes the attestation, so ask the office for it.
steps.deadline: On or before the 20th day of the month following the tax month
steps.fee: 6.7% of net gross receipts; late payment penalty 10% of the tax due, plus interest at 10% per annum
steps.quote: To avoid penalty and/or interest, this return with payment must be filed on or before the 20th day of the month following the tax month.

steps.step: Account for Virginia sales tax on stays you book directly
steps.who: Operator for direct bookings; platforms for the bookings they facilitate
steps.how: Lodging is also subject to Virginia retail sales tax, listed by the City at 5.3%. For stays you book yourself, you collect it and pay it to the Virginia Department of Taxation, which means registering with the Department as a dealer. This state process is not modeled here.
steps.fee: 5.3% (state retail sales tax, as listed by the City)
steps.quote: Every individual, partnership, corporation, etc. engaging in business as a retail dealer in Virginia is required to register with the Department of Taxation, P O Box 6-L Richmond, VA. 23282 to obtain a Certificate of Registration.

steps.step: Report the rental's furnishings as business personal property
steps.how: Staunton taxes furniture, fixtures and equipment used in a business. If the Commissioner treats your homestay as a business, list those items with their purchase dates and original costs on the annual business personal property return. See the separate process business_tangible_personal_property_return.
steps.deadline: By May 1 each year (payment due December 5)
steps.fee: Business personal property tax, billed later by the City Treasurer
steps.quote: The City of Staunton levies a tax on tangible personal property employed in a trade or business, including furniture, fixtures, equipment, machinery, tools, etc.

steps.step: Renew the registration and the business license by March 1 every year
steps.how: By March 1, register again for each property: give your full name and each property's legal and street address and parcel number, and pay $50 per property. Renew the business license by the same date on the City's renewal form, reporting last year's actual gross receipts. Its rate table includes the Homestay Yearly Registration at $50.00. Filings received or postmarked after March 1 are late. When March 1 falls on a weekend or holiday, state law lets the filing be made on the next business day (Va. Code § 1-210(E)), and the Taxes page says payments are then accepted the next business day without penalty. March 1, 2026 was a Sunday, yet the 2026 form set the penalty date at March 2, which conflicts with both; ask the office if this affects you.
steps.deadline: Not later than March 1 each year
steps.fee: $50.00 per property, plus the business license fee or tax; late license filing: 10% penalty, then interest at 10% per annum
steps.quote: After initial registration under the provision of this chapter, a short-term rental operator shall register by not later than March 1 each year with the Commissioner of Revenue, providing the complete name of the operator and the legal and street address (and parcel identification number) of each property in the City of Staunton offered for short-term rental by the operator.

steps.who: Operator; Commissioner of the Revenue; Zoning Administrator
steps.how: Failing to register costs $500 for each violation. Until you pay it and register, you may not offer or rent the property. Repeated violations of the registration chapter for a property bar the operator from registering and offering it, and so do violations of state and local short-term rental laws on more than three occasions. Breaking the homestay zoning rules is a zoning violation: City Code § 18.225.010 (read on eCode360, paraphrased) punishes it on conviction with a $50 fine plus costs, each day a separate offense, and the City may also seek an injunction (state law caps such fines at $1,000, Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(5)). Doing business without a required license is a Class 4 misdemeanor (City Code § 5.05.020(1), paraphrased). Intentionally failing to file a lodging tax report is a misdemeanor, and if no report is filed the Commissioner may determine the tax due after notice and a chance to be heard (City Code §§ 3.35.100, 3.35.070, paraphrased).
steps.fee: $500.00 per violation for failing to register
steps.quote: There is imposed a penalty of $500.00 for each violation for any failure to register as required under the provision of this chapter.

steps.step: Close the accounts if you stop hosting
steps.how: If you stop, write the date you stopped in box (1) of the business license renewal, sign it and return it to the Commissioner. Under City Code § 3.35.080 (read on eCode360, paraphrased), when you quit, any lodging tax becomes due at once and you must immediately file a report and pay it. The pages read give no closure step for the registration, so tell the office in writing and ask how to close the registration and the lodging tax account.
steps.quote: IF YOU ARE NO LONGER IN BUSINESS, provide the date you ceased to operate, sign below and return this renewal to our office.

escalation.trigger: Homestay registration refused or not processed, although the form is complete and the fee paid
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue: ask in writing for the reason and point out that a registry is ministerial
escalation.quote: The registration shall be ministerial in nature and shall require the operator to provide (i) the complete name of the operator, (ii) the address of each property in the locality offered for short-term rental by the operator, and (iii) an attestation that the property owner has granted permission for use of such property as a short-term rental if the operator is a lessee or sublessee.

escalation.trigger: Registration still refused with no lawful ground
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court: petition for a writ of mandamus to compel the ministerial act
escalation.quote: application for a writ of mandamus or a writ of prohibition shall be on petition verified by oath

escalation.trigger: Zoning Administrator's written order, notice of violation or determination about the homestay (for example that the use is not allowed or breaks Chapter 18.152)
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals (file a notice of appeal, giving the grounds, with the Zoning Administrator and the Board, through Planning & Zoning; fee $200). The Board presumes the Zoning Administrator's determination correct, and the appellant must rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence (City Code § 18.200.020, paraphrased).
escalation.deadline: 30 days after the decision, after which it is final and unappealable; 10 days for a notice of violation for short-term, recurring violations such as maximum occupancy limits of a dwelling (City Code § 18.200.020(5), paraphrased; allowed by Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4)). The period does not start until the written notice stating the appeal right is sent by registered or certified mail or posted.
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

escalation.trigger: No answer from the Zoning Administrator to a written request for a zoning determination
escalation.next: Zoning Administrator, reminded of the 90-day duty to respond; the statute gives no deemed approval
escalation.deadline: 90 days from the request, unless the requester agreed to longer
escalation.quote: The zoning administrator shall respond within 90 days of a request for a decision or determination on zoning matters within the scope of his authority unless the requester has agreed to a longer period.

escalation.trigger: Board of Zoning Appeals decides against you
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court (petition filed with the clerk)
escalation.deadline: 30 days after the Board's final decision (mandatory and jurisdictional)
escalation.quote: may, within 30 days after the final decision of the board, file with the clerk of the circuit court for the county or city a petition that shall be styled

escalation.trigger: Lodging tax, penalty or other local tax assessment you think is wrong
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (application for correction)
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment, whichever is later
escalation.quote: apply to the commissioner of the revenue or such other official who made the assessment for a correction thereof.

escalation.trigger: Business license tax assessment, or the license classification applied to the homestay, you think is wrong
escalation.next: Commissioner of the Revenue (administrative appeal, in good faith, identifying the tax periods, the amount in dispute, each alleged error and the remedy sought)
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the appealable event, whichever is later
escalation.quote: may file an administrative appeal of the assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event, whichever is later, with the commissioner of the revenue or other local assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Business license tax or classification decided against you on administrative appeal
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner, Virginia Department of Taxation (serve a copy on the Commissioner of the Revenue)
escalation.deadline: 90 days from the Commissioner of the Revenue's determination
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment or determination to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the date of the determination by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Correction refused (lodging tax) or Tax Commissioner decides against you (license tax)
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court (application for relief from an erroneous assessment)
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, or one year from the Tax Commissioner's or local final determination, whichever is later
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, so the city pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them or by phone before you act.

Local law. The Staunton City Code is published on eCode360 (General Code). Its Terms of Use forbid copying or republishing content for public purposes, so no City Code text from eCode360 is quoted, and the City Code points marked 'paraphrased' come from it. The quotes from chapters 3.37 and 18.152 come from the back of the City's own Homestay Registration form (PDF created January 2018, the same file in the 2021, 2022 and 2025 captures, and still the form linked in the August 2026 capture). The eCode360 text of both chapters has the same substance, with editorial differences, and no uncodified New Law was listed for them on 2026-10-11. eCode360 says its copy may not reflect the latest legislation.

Zoning. Chapter 18.152 sets homestay rules and says it prescribes the conditions under which the use is allowed. The district chapters on eCode360 (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, TRD-1, TND-I, P-1, B-1, B-2, B-4, B-5) and the standards for uses permitted on review (ch. 18.105) do not mention homestays, and the Planning & Zoning permit list has no homestay permit. Other districts (R-5, R-6, I-1 to I-3, the Entrance Corridor overlay, H-1, HE-1 and A-1) were not read. So it is not known how the City applies chapter 18.152 district by district, or whether a zoning permit is ever required. Ask Planning & Zoning, or request a Zoning Official Determination Letter ($75). For owner-occupied primary residences, state law bars special use permit requirements only in ordinances enacted or amended after December 31, 2023 (Va. Code § 15.2-983(D)).

Owner occupancy and tenants. The City's printed text has no owner-occupancy rule, and its definition of operator includes lessees. State law requires a registry to collect the owner's permission when a tenant registers. The City's form has an owner signature line marked 'if applicable' and no separate attestation.

Registration and business license. The City's pages do not say whether a homestay host must also file the Business License Application, or which license class and rate apply. The rate table lists only the $50 Homestay Yearly Registration. City Code § 3.37.030(1) says registration allows the assessment of the business license required under § 5.05.100, which (paraphrased) requires a license of anyone with a definite place of business in the city. State law bars license taxes on renting real property other than hotels, bed and breakfasts, lodging houses, rooming houses and similar uses (Va. Code § 58.1-3703(C)(7)); whether Staunton treats a homestay as one of those was not found. Ask the Commissioner.

Exemptions. Va. Code § 15.2-983(B)(2) bars registration requirements for some operators: those licensed by the Real Estate Board or owners represented by a real estate licensee, time-share registrants, those licensed or registered with the Department of Health for lodging, and those licensed or registered with the locality for renting or managing real property (such as hotels, motels and bed and breakfasts). The City's printed chapter 3.37 lists no exemptions. Whether the City applies the state exemptions, and whether exempt operators still owe the license and lodging tax, was not confirmed.

30-day boundary. The definitions differ. City Code § 3.37.020 and state law define a short-term rental as fewer than 30 consecutive days. The homestay definition in § 18.152.020 allows stays of up to 30 days. The lodging tax return's line 2a exempts only rentals of more than 30 consecutive days, but City Code §§ 3.35.010 and 3.35.020 (paraphrased) levy the tax on transients, defined as people staying fewer than 30 consecutive days, so the ordinance does not appear to tax a stay of exactly 30 days. Ask the Commissioner how the return treats it.

Platform bookings. City Code § 3.35.040 (paraphrased) has the platform collect and remit the tax on bookings it facilitates, and § 3.35.050(6) (paraphrased) lets a host whose sales are all facilitated by platforms attest to that instead of reporting, as Va. Code § 58.1-3827(D) allows. No City page or form read mentions the attestation, and the City's return asks hosts to report platform receipts and deduct the tax the platform paid, with documents. The state-law quotes on intermediaries come from the county article (Va. Code § 58.1-3826), which reaches a city's tax through § 58.1-3843(C); the City Code now says the same in its own terms.

Lodging tax penalty. The City's return applies a flat 10% late-payment penalty. State law allows up to 10% for the first month and 5% a month after, up to 25%, if an ordinance provides it (Va. Code § 58.1-3916). Chapter 3.35 as read on eCode360 provides interest at 10% a year (§ 3.35.060) and a misdemeanor for intentionally failing to file (§ 3.35.100), but no percentage penalty, and the penalty in § 3.10.040, as far as read, concerns the real estate and personal property tax dates. The local basis for the return's 10% penalty was not found.

Decisions and deadlines. No time limit was found for the Commissioner to act on a registration. Nor was any procedure for imposing the $500 penalty or for the bar on repeat violators (City Code § 3.37.060). The form says the 'permit may be revoked', but the printed chapter has no revocation clause. The mandamus route in the escalation is the general remedy for a refused ministerial act. Case law on it is not covered here.
Business personal property. The City taxes furniture and equipment used in a business, but no page says how it treats a homestay's furnishings. Ask the Commissioner.

Board of Zoning Appeals. The City's boards site (stauntonva.granicus.com) refuses automated readers, so the Board's page is not described here. The appeal rules come from Va. Code § 15.2-2311 and City Code § 18.200.020 (paraphrased), which sets a 10-day appeal period for notices of short-term, recurring violations such as occupancy limits; whether the City treats a given homestay notice that way will show on the notice, which must state the appeal period. The appeal form cited is an older version under the former 'Department of Planning & Inspections' name. Confirm its P.O. Box 581 filing address with Planning & Zoning; the Start a Business page gives P.O. Box 58 for the Building Official.

Privacy. The forms and the Commissioner's page name the elected Commissioner, and the Planning & Zoning page names staff and gives personal staff mailboxes, including the Zoning Administrator's mailbox for zoning complaints. None of these is recorded; only office phones, addresses and the office mailbox printed on the forms are.

Online filing. No online route for homestay registration or lodging tax returns was found on the pages read; the forms say to mail, fax or email. The City's online permitting portal and the Treasurer's self-service portal were not opened.

Wrong form risk. The Local Tax Forms page also lists a 'Short Term Tax Form', a Short Term Rental Tax Return charging 1% on rentals of 92 days or less, filed quarterly. It is for the City's short-term rental property tax on businesses renting tangible personal property (City Code § 5.05.230, paraphrased; Va. Code § 58.1-3510.6), not for lodging. Homestay hosts use the Transient/Occupancy Tax Return.

Brochure. The City's new business brochure (Internet Archive copy of 2025-09-17) says the occupancy tax applies to a lodging place that furnishes lodging to 'four or more transients'. The Start a Business page and City Code § 3.35.010 (paraphrased; amended by Ord. 2021-33 and 2022-24) cover lodging furnished to any transients. The brochure appears out of date; do not rely on it to skip the lodging tax.

corrections: Quotes: all 81 draft quotes were confirmed word for word. The 37 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited sections (whitespace normalised), and their subsection labels match the text. The 44 City quotes were found in Internet Archive copies of the cited www.ci.staunton.va.us pages and PDFs, re-fetched read-only with the research User-Agent (the live site still answers HTTP 403, robots.txt included): Homestay Registration PDF (2025-09-17 capture, same file digest as the 2021 and 2022 captures), Business License & Taxes (2026-08-09), Business License Application (2025-09-17), 2026 renewal (2026-06-07), Taxes (2026-08-22), Transient/Occupancy Tax Return (2025-10-14), Start a Business (2026-07-17) and Planning & Zoning Fees (2026-05-10). The section sign in the PDF's 'SCC §5.05.100' and 'SCC §3.35.010' does not extract as text; it was confirmed on a rendered image of page 2. Six quotes were added and checked the same way (Va. Code §§ 15.2-2286(A)(4), 15.2-2311(A), 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(b), in legal_basis and in a new escalation rung, 1-210(E), and the Taxes page's next-business-day rule). lexflow's check_quotes matches 42 of 42 state-code quotes in the final file.

Zoning appeal deadline (escalation): the rung gave only 30 days. City Code § 18.200.020(5) (read on eCode360, paraphrased) sets a 10-day appeal period for notices of short-term, recurring violations, including maximum occupancy limits of a dwelling, as Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4) allows. Added, with the rule that an unappealed decision is final and unappealable and that the period starts only when the notice stating the appeal right is sent by registered or certified mail or posted (§ 15.2-2311(A)), and the Board's presumption that the Zoning Administrator is correct (§ 18.200.020(1), (2)). Two state-law quotes added to legal_basis.

s12: 'Staunton's own zoning penalty section was not read' replaced with City Code § 18.225.010 (paraphrased): a $50 fine plus costs on conviction, each day a separate offense, and injunction. Added that doing business without a required license is a Class 4 misdemeanor (§ 5.05.020(1)), that intentionally failing to file a lodging tax report is a misdemeanor (§ 3.35.100), and that the Commissioner may determine the tax due after notice and a chance to be heard (§ 3.35.070). 'Can bar the property' now follows § 3.37.060(2) and (3), which say the operator 'is prohibited'.

s8, summary and the platform caveat: the draft said no Staunton source mentions the platform-only attestation. City Code § 3.35.050(6) (paraphrased) provides it: 12 months at a time, renewed yearly on a date and form the Commissioner sets. Reworded; the City's pages and forms still do not describe it.

30-day boundary caveat: the draft concluded that a stay of exactly 30 days appears taxable. City Code §§ 3.35.010 and 3.35.020 (paraphrased) levy the tax on transients, defined as people staying fewer than 30 consecutive days; rewritten to say the ordinance does not appear to reach a 30-day stay, although the return's wording suggests otherwise.
s13: added City Code § 3.35.080 (paraphrased): on quitting, the lodging tax is due at once with a final report.

s11 and the late-renewal fee entry: the draft noted without comment that the 2026 form set the penalty date at March 2 because March 1 was a Sunday. Va. Code § 1-210(E) lets a filing due on a day the office is closed be made the next business day, and the Taxes page says payments are then accepted without penalty, so the form's date conflicts with both. Added, with a state-law quote and a City quote.

s5, summary and the business license fee entry: 'for the classes the City lists, the fee is $30 up to $50,000' was too broad; the rate table charges wholesale merchants $100 and direct sellers differently. Now names the contractor, retail, professional and business service classes. Added City Code § 5.05.060 (no license where zoning prohibits the business), § 5.05.020(2) (the delinquent taxes include transient occupancy and meals taxes) and § 5.05.100(2) (apply before beginning business), all paraphrased.

s1: the draft said the rules apply to an 'owner, tenant or manager'; the City's operator definition lists owner, lessee, sub-lessee, mortgagee in possession, licensee or other possessory capacity, not a manager. Reworded. The zoning sentence now reports the district chapters read on eCode360 (none mentions homestays) and the Planning & Zoning permit list (no homestay permit).
s3: the 24/7 responsible party is a requirement of the form; the printed chapter 3.37 does not mention it and it is not among the items Va. Code § 15.2-983(B)(1) says a registry requires. Said so.

s6: 'The Zoning Administrator may inspect ... at least once a year' reworded to follow § 18.152.030(5): at the Zoning Administrator's request the operator must allow entry, on reasonable notice, at least once each calendar year.

Escalation: added the business license administrative appeal to the Commissioner (Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(b): within one year from the last day of the tax year or from the appealable event, whichever is later), which the Tax Commissioner rung presupposes; the correction rung (§ 58.1-3980) now covers the lodging tax, penalties and other local taxes.

Legal basis: the homestay-definition entry no longer says the Business License & Taxes page cites § 18.152.020 (it gives the words without a section number). Added local entries without quotes for the City Code chapters read on eCode360 for reference (currency of 3.37 and 18.152, chapter 3.35, chapter 5.05 Article IA, § 5.05.230, § 18.200.020(5), § 18.225.010).

Caveats: updated Access, Local law (chapters 3.37 and 18.152 on eCode360 match the form in substance; no New Law listed for them), Zoning, Registration and business license, Exemptions (all four state exemptions), Lodging tax penalty (chapter 3.35 states interest but no percentage penalty) and Board of Zoning Appeals. Added two caveats: the Local Tax Forms page's 'Short Term Tax Form' is a 1% quarterly return for renting tangible personal property (City Code § 5.05.230; Va. Code § 58.1-3510.6), not for lodging; and the new business brochure's 'four or more transients' limit is out of step with the current ordinance and the Start a Business page.
Sources: added the new business brochure and the Short Term Rental Tax Return (Internet Archive copies), the eCode360 Code, and Va. Code §§ 1-210 and 58.1-3510.6.
